about: Reviewed detections, by ATT&CK technique. Each one keys on what the technique does, never on the test marker. 'single' matches one command line; 'burst' needs several different tools from the same host within a short time. The SPL rendered from an entry is a starting point for the reviewer, not a finished rule.

detections.title: Several discovery tools from one host within five minutes
detections.why: One discovery command is ordinary admin work. Several different ones from the same host within minutes is what an intruder's first look around looks like.

detections.title: whoami run
detections.why: Reads the current user and its groups.

detections.title: arp -a run
detections.why: Reads the table of recently seen neighbours.

detections.title: Port proxy tool used
detections.why: The port proxy part of netsh is rarely used in normal work and is a common way to relay traffic through a host.

no_behaviour.echo_marker: This step only prints the marker. There is nothing a real rule could key on except the marker itself.
no_behaviour.ps_echo_marker: This step only prints the marker. There is nothing a real rule could key on except the marker itself.
no_behaviour.drop_marker_file: An empty file in the temp folder is too ordinary to detect by itself; the marker in its name is what makes it stand out.
no_behaviour.dns_lookup_marker: The looked-up name is special only because of the marker and the reserved test domain.
